build.name: a finished lesson names the words it taught
a unit test says whether it passed and whether it was taken early

note: The course events (`build`: what coursePayload writes for its input, member order included) and the derivation of a learner's path state (#221, README "Derivation"): a filled course (only the members the derivation reads: section and unit ids, a unit's test, its words' keys and its lessons), one workspace's stored events of every type, the words the learner has marked known, and the state. The course id is `zh-test`. Go: server/internal/courses/derive_contract_test.go (Derive); web: apps/web/src/lib/studycore/courseProgress.test.ts (deriveCourseState).

cases.name: no events: the first lesson of the first unit is next
lessons finish in order; a unit without a test is done when its lessons are; a unit whose lessons are done waits for its test
a passed unit test closes the unit and opens the next
a failed test changes nothing; a started lesson is marked
an early unit test skips that unit and every unit before it; their words not met or known are output as known
a passed section exam skips its section and every unit before it; a failed one does nothing
a placement skips the sections before it; words met before stay met, not known
events of another type or course and malformed events are ignored
cases.note: a grammar event; another course; an unknown kind; score above total; a unit test without passed; a ts that is not RFC 3339; an empty word key; a section id that is not an id

cases.name: events replay in (ts, id) order, not in arrival order
cases.note: Sorted: the lesson (09:59), then in the same second the lower id: u1's own test (studied), then u2's early test, which skips intro and u2 but not u1, already passed. u1's unmet c becomes a catch-up lesson, not a known word. In arrival order u1 would have been skipped and c known.
